text:
incident-bot: PAGER — P0: serving-runtime: repeated CUDA OOMs + container crashloops in eu-central-1. Autoscaler reacting aggressively -> scale thrash + brownout. Paging oncall: @maria, escalate to infra @ajay, runtime @kevin, SRE @elaine :rotating_light:
maria: acked. joining bridge now. seeing spike in pod restarts in model-pool-gpu-eu (p90 restart rate ~ 42/min).
ajay: adding context — we had a node-image rolling upgrade earlier today; some nodes show driver 525.x, others 530.x. suspect driver/compat issue.
kevin: logs from crashed containers show repeated allocation failures: `E CudaDriver: cudnnAlloc failed: out of memory` + `segfault` while loading KV cache. posting sample logs:
```
[2026-03-15T10:12:03Z] model-server[pid=42]: failed to allocate cuda memory: CUDNN_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED
[2026-03-15T10:12:03Z] model-server[pid=42]: terminating process, exit code 139
```
elaine: we're also seeing HPA scale events every ~30s tied to a custom throughput metric — HPA jumps from 8->40 pods then crashbacks when nodes evict. looks exactly like autoscaler feedback loop.
maria: immediate mitigation plan: 1) pause HPA/autoscaler 2) pin min replicas to current stable count 3) cordon any nodes with mismatched driver 4) fallback routing to smaller model variant for latency-sensitive customers. assigning tasks.
ajay: on it — cordoning suspicious nodes now. command:
```sh
kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep gpu | awk '$5 ~ /530/ {print $1}' | xargs -r kubectl cordon
```
kevin: disabling autoscaling on the model-pool group (scaledown disabled) and setting minReplicas=10 to stop oscillation. applying: `kubectl patch hpa model-pool-hpa -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":10,"behavior":null}}'`
elaine: rolling back the node image to driver 525 on a small node set looks risky. alternative: migrate pods off 530 nodes and drain. Ajay, can you taint them so scheduler avoids them?
ajay: taint applied: `kubectl taint nodes gpu-530-* node-role.kubernetes.io/evict=:NoSchedule` — draining started for 3 nodes.
kevin: recommending to route new traffic to a warm fallback model `gpt-medium-stable-v2` which is CPU-backed and has smaller GPU memory footprint. updating replica set to maintain warm instances.
maria: notify CS + customers affected: CS list shows three enterprise customers using low-latency endpoints in eu region. @cs-team please prepare templated message, impact = degraded throughput, some 5xxs.
cs-team: Preparing message. ETA 10m. Will indicate degraded performance and active mitigation.
elaine: after draining 3 nodes, pod restart rate dropped ~60%. however autoscaler metrics still reflect spikes because of leftover queued requests — HPA is paused but cluster-autoscaler loop still sees pending pods. need to suspend cluster-autoscaler too.
ajay: suspended cluster-autoscaler for the model pool. command: `kubectl scale deployment cluster-autoscaler --replicas=0 -n kube-system` (we are running a dedicated CA in that namespace).
kevin: observed one class of failures different from OOM — `mmap` errors when loading mmap'd shards right after pod start. looks like concurrent startups hitting GPU memory allocation race. Mitigation: enable staggered startup by adding a startupDelaySeconds=10 in node-affinity init. Applying a quick patch to statefulset to add `initContainer` sleep for jitter.
maria: good. Also enabling eviction protection for warm pods: `kubectl annotate pod <pod> eviction.kubernetes.io/protected=true`. Doing that for top 10 warm replicas.
incident-bot: NOTE: autoscaling actions in progress — HPA paused, CA scaled to 0, nodes cordoned/drained, traffic reroute to fallback model.
ajay: interesting observation — one node had NVIDIA driver crash messages in dmesg referencing `nvlddmkm` and the kernel OOPS before container OOMs. pushing kernel logs to /var/logs/incident/gpu-node-7.log.
kevin: suggested hotfix: pin runtime to use CUDA 11.8 compatible runtime image and disable cudnn autotune for the short term (reduces frag, minor perf hit). patching image tag to `redwood/runtime:release-2026-03-cuda11.8` on the canary subset.
elaine: after canary roll, can we re-enable autoscaler with dampening? we should set scaleDown/scaleUp stabilization windows to avoid immediate thrash. proposal: scaleUp stabilization 5m, scaleDown stabilization 10m.
maria: agreed. After we see canary stable for 8 minutes, re-enable CA with stabilization parameters.
ajay: draining completed; 3 bad nodes out of pool. marking them for reprovision.
kevin: canary patch rolled to 5% — no crashes for 7 minutes, memory allocation patterns normalized.
cs-team: initial customer message sent: "We are experiencing degraded throughput in EU; mitigation underway; no data loss; next update in 30m."
maria: status update to execs in 20m. Postmortem owners: @kevin (runtime), @ajay (infra), @elaine (sre).
elaine: follow-ups item list: - investigate driver mismatch rollout gating - add autoscaler damping defaults to platform - add startup jitter and memory guard checks - alert on rapid HPA oscillation
kevin: saving heap/kv-cache core dumps for failed containers to S3 path: s3://redwood-incident-dumps/2175001234/ for later analysis.
maria: incident status: mitigation successful for now. brownout avoided, customer impact reduced to intermittent 5xxs for 3 customers. keeping incident open for verification until 2026-03-15T11:30Z.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation actions applied. next automated update in 30m. :white_check_mark:
